newsitem.title: FRANCE: CDR sees 40 bln Fr of assets sales in 1996 - paper.
newsitem.headline: CDR sees 40 bln Fr of assets sales in 1996 - paper.

text.p: French state-backed rescue vehicle Consortium de Realisation (CDR) expects to have sold about 40 billion francs ($7.7 billion) of assets this year and is on track for disposing two thirds of its portfolio by the end of 1998, its managing director said in remarks published on Tuesday.
"Some 40 billion francs of the assets at least should be sold in 1996, out of 158 billion francs on our books on the January 1, 1996," Francois Lemasson said in an interview with newspaper Le Monde.
CDR is the holding company set up in 1995 charged with selling assets of struggling bank Credit Lyonnais.
He said the sales in 1996 represented a fairly marked speeding up of the disposal process. CDR sold 25 billion francs of assets last year.
"CDR is in line with chairman Michel Rouger's objectives, that is to have reduced the portfolio by two-thirds at the end of 1998"

CDR will reduce its stake to 15 percent in the new company to be formed from the present merger between French computer services company Sligos and Axime, another systems house, he said. CDR could gradually sell its remaining holding in the market, he added.
CDR currently owns 56.8 percent of Sligos. It said in January it planned to hold on to its stake for two years to allow Sligos to complete a restructuring.
CDR has sold stakes in other companies, he said.

"The unwinding of cross-shareholding agreements has allowed sales of some holdings, such as Total SA, or in more uncomfortable and less favourable conditions, Cie Navigation Mixte," he said. "We have also sold over time other stakes such as Lagardere."
